blocks.title: Commercial Engine
blocks.body: Aloft Hotels commercial distribution rides Marriott Bonvoy direct channels, GDS, OTAs, and parent sales systems. Select-service lifestyle: modern rooms, social lobby energy, and tech-forward cues for urban and airport-adjacent travelers inside Marriott Bonvoy. Owners should underwrite channel mix and loyalty contribution for this asset—not corporate averages alone.

blocks.title: Commercial Differentiator
blocks.body: Versus Moxy's budget lifestyle intensity and AC Hotels' European contemporary select-service, Aloft sits in modern lifestyle select-service without W-level luxury capital.

blocks.body: Aloft Hotels demand follows destination seasonality plus Marriott Bonvoy campaign calendars. Treat portfolio averages as directional; diligence this hotel's source markets and corporate vs leisure mix.

blocks.title: Marriott Bonvoy
blocks.body: Aloft Hotels participates in Marriott Bonvoy. Members earn and redeem points and receive Elite recognition across participating sister brands. Confirm current tier names and earn rules on the official program site before IC.

blocks.body: Guests earn Marriott Bonvoy points on qualifying stays at Aloft Hotels. Elite members may receive enhanced earn and recognition benefits per current program rules.

blocks.title: Redeem
blocks.body: Points redeem for stays across the Marriott Bonvoy portfolio, including Aloft Hotels, subject to availability and current redemption charts.

blocks.title: Elite Recognition
blocks.body: Elite status recognition (upgrades, late checkout, lounge access where offered) applies per property capability—delivery varies by hotel.

blocks.title: Ecosystem

blocks.title: Owner Lens

blocks.body: Front desk and systems must support Marriott Bonvoy enrollment, Elite recognition, and redemption stays without erasing the brand's guest experience.

blocks.title: Systems Implications

blocks.title: Repeat Guest Capture
blocks.body: Marriott Bonvoy earn and recognition increase the probability of repeat Aloft stays where the hotel already competes on product fit—not on a standardized prototype alone.

blocks.body: Bonvoy member rates and Marriott direct paths help Aloft hotels defend contribution against high-commission intermediaries while keeping brand positioning intact.

blocks.body: Renewal PIP; conversion PIP revisions; transfer / change-of-ownership fees; termination-related obligations; owner-funded reserves—triggered at renewal, repositioning, or exit. Confirm liquidated damages and transfer mechanics in the current agreement.

blocks.body: Initial vs conversion paths differ; program contribution and loyalty assessments may change by year under agreement terms. Lock the fee exhibit before IC—never extrapolate from a peer hotel's rumor. Geography note: Confirm current Marriott franchise / development disclosure for Aloft

blocks.title: Why Value Is Strongest in These Scenarios
blocks.body:
Keep Local Product Intent—Add Marriott Bonvoy: retain Aloft Hotels's brand promise while accessing loyalty earn/redeem and parent commercial systems a standalone hotel cannot buy alone.
Select-service lifestyle: modern rooms, social lobby energy, and tech-forward cues for urban and airport-adjacent travelers inside Marriott Bonvoy.
Sibling Clarity: diligence fit versus same-parent peers before assuming identical owner use case or fee path.
Operator & Owner Fit: strongest when the asset can deliver the brand's guest promise with QA discipline—weakest when sponsors want the flag without the product investment.
Disclosure Discipline: model economics only from current fee exhibits—Factory 2.0 does not invent undisclosed percentages.
